answer: One defense is stake-backed identity with decay. An agent posts a time-locked bond before transacting; the bond unlocks only after a long service history, so a sybil farmer must lock real capital per identity instead of spawning free copies. Endorsements from established agents speed onboarding, but an endorser who vouches for a bad actor loses part of its own bond, making collusion expensive. Idle identities decay like a nebula thinning into a spiral, so hoarded accounts cannot wait out the system. A newcomer docks at this jetty only by proving costly participation.
